title: Gateway request-stampede mitigation and quota-enforcer hardening
creator: Maya Patel
description: Follow-up actions from the Feb 26th 429 spike where a burst of simultaneous token revalidations caused the gateway quota-enforcer to overcount active tokens and return elevated 429 rates. This ticket bundles code fixes, fallback policies, and observability improvements to prevent recurrence and reduce blast radius for future auth/cache-related stampedes.
timeline_summary: 02/26: ~11:40 UTC - traffic surge with correlated auth refreshes. 11:42 - first sustained 429 spike; 11:55 - mitigation rolled by throttling back aggressive enforcer refresh. 12:30 - full service recovery after deploying staged cache-TTL increase and temporary lenient enforcement policy. Feb 27-03/01 - initial RCA and triage. Mar 02 - prioritized follow-ups and owner assignments.
root_cause: A misaligned combination of short-lived auth TTLs and synchronous token validation on gateway edge nodes led to simultaneous cache misses; quota-enforcer rebounded by aggressively renewing counts without coordinated de-duplication, producing transient over-enforcement. Additionally, the enforcer lacked jittered exponential backoff when contacting the auth cache under high miss rates.
impact_details: Approximately 18 minutes of elevated 429s for 12% of requests across EU and us-west regions; several mid-market customers reported degraded UX for streaming generation, and a small set of webhooks retried heavily, contributing to downstream load. No data loss or secret leaks detected.
mitigations_applied_during_incident: - Increased auth cache TTL on gateway nodes to 30s temporarily. - Deployed a lenient quota-enforcement fallback that allowed best-effort routing for requests marked internal. - Manually scaled gateway pool in us-west region by +20% capacity. - Enabled request jitter on client retries via the edge proxy config.
action_items: Code: Add request de-duplication layer in quota-enforcer to squash concurrent token validations (owner: Daniel Chen, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4821)
Code: Implement jittered exponential backoff for enforcer auth-cache fetches and mark retriable paths (owner: Priya Singh, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4834)
Config: Default auth cache TTL increase to 45s with region-specific tuning and a runtime flag for fast rollback (owner: Infra Config, RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GW/Auth+TTL+Proposal)

Policy: Add staged enforcement policy that automatically ramps enforcement thresholds when sustained cache-miss rates exceed 5% for >2m (owner: Reliability, runbook updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/gateway-enforcement-runbook)

Observability: Add high-cardinality metric for 'concurrent-token-validations' and dashboard panel with alert thresholds (owner: Observability, dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/gateway-token-stampede)

Testing: Add chaos test that simulates synchronized TTL expirations across 80% of nodes and validates enforcement behavior (owner: SRE, test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sre-chaos/tree/eng-21750)
Customer comms: Draft targeted post-incident note for affected customers and update status page incident postmortem (owner: Support, draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c)
Post-deploy: Run 72h validation with canary traffic profile and token-refresh simulator before fully rolling new enforcer (owner: Release Engineering)
Long-term: Explore moving quota accounting to a lightweight distributed counter with conflict-free replication to reduce hot-spotting (owner: Research/Applied ML)
Follow-up ticket: Break out performance regression tests for token-bucket alignment edge cases (create ENG-21790)
acceptance_criteria: Code merged and deployed to canary; canary shows <1% additional 429s under synthetic token-refresh bursts; alerts fire for concurrent-token-validations > 50 with automatic mitigation enabled; config flag allows immediate rollback.

03/08 - QA: Added regression test matrix across sequence lengths and client library retry strategies.

resolution_summary: In-progress. Short-term mitigations successfully lowered immediate customer impact. Primary code changes and observability are under review; planned canary deploy scheduled. Long-term architecture improvements scoped.
